function: MIMO-OFDM symbol detection: windowed echo state network (WESN) equalizes the received signal, with input and reservoir weights configured from channel statistics (pp. 1, 4).
system: 4x4 MIMO-OFDM with ULAs at both ends (also SISO OFDM), 1024 subcarriers, 3.5 GHz (band n78), 16-QAM; no RIS (pp. 11, 13).
method: Reservoir computing (windowed ESN, an RNN): input and reservoir weights configured by PCA of channel statistics; readout trained online by supervised least squares per slot (pp. 2, 6).
data_channel: Simulated 3GPP CDL-D and CDL-E (TR 38.901) and SCM (TR 25.996) LOS channels; readout trained on the slot's reference signals, BER measured on data symbols (pp. 11-13).
test_conditions: No train/test mismatch reported; readout retrained each slot (p. 2). Evaluated at 5 and 20 km/h, CDL-D and CDL-E LOS profiles; NLOS left to future work (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Non-learned: em-LMMSE channel estimation with LMMSE equalization; learned: WESN with randomly generated weights from earlier work [5] (pp. 2, 12, 13).
metrics: BER versus Eb/N0 (16-QAM); run time in seconds (Table I); normalized approximation error of Theorem 1 versus M (pp. 7, 11, 13).
complexity: O(Nsc^3) worst case to compute configured weights; WESN FLOPs expression; measured weight computation 0.540 s (FD), 0.764 s (TD); LMMSE baseline 3.798/51.846 s (pp. 10, 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "channel model [34], specifically CDL-D and CDL"; reference [34] is p. 16: "Standard TR 38.901, 3GPP". The 4x4 channel uses the 3GPP SCM [30] with CDL power delay profiles (pp. 13-14).
q2_support: p. 2: "within each new slot using the limited OTA RSs" (the detector is retrained every slot). Not met: no model trained in one scenario, band or configuration is tested in another; the 20 km/h case (p. 14) is a separate evaluation and NLOS is future work (p. 12).
q3_support: p. 14: "time than the baseline non-learning approach" (LMMSE+LMMSE-Interpolated-CSI, p. 13); p. 12: "further divided into WESN with randomly generated weights" (WESN is the earlier method of [5], p. 2). BER curves in Figs. 13-17 (pp. 13-14).
q4_support: p. 11: "of computing configured weights is O(Nsc" (O(Nsc^3), worst case); Table I on the same page lists measured run times in seconds; p. 10 gives the WESN FLOPs expression.
q5_support: p. 11: "verified through extensive simulations for both OFDM and 4 × 4 MIMO-OFDM systems" on simulated 3GPP channels; no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data anywhere in the paper (pp. 1-17).
notes: Included, area 1: MIMO-OFDM symbol detection, BER is the main metric (p. 1). The learned element is the WESN, an RNN whose readout is trained per slot (p. 2) and whose other weights are configured from channel statistics by PCA (p. 4). q1: CDL-D/E of TR 38.901 (p. 11); the 4x4 channel follows 3GPP SCM TR 25.996 [30], another standardized model for the reviewer to confirm (p. 13). q3 is borderline: the learned baseline is the earlier WESN of [5] with random weights, which is also the proposed detector without configured weights; no other learned detector is compared. Table I values were read from the PDF image (p. 11).
